sections.content: How many people are "production managers and directors in mining and energy"?

18,830 people

were counted on the census as "production managers and directors in mining and energy" in England and Wales in March 2021.

Production managers and directors in mining, energy and water supply organise and co-ordinate the activities and resources necessary for the extraction of minerals and other natural deposits, the utilisation of sustainable and renewable energy sources and the production, storage and provision of gas, water and electricity supplies.

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "production managers and directors in mining and energy" there were more men than women (80.1% compared with 19.9%).

This means "production managers and directors in mining and energy" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "corporate managers and directors".

Men made up 80.1% and women made up 19.9% of "production managers and directors in mining and energy"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "production managers and directors in mining and energy" included:

  • managers in storage and warehousing
  • elementary storage occupations (other)
  • information technology professionals (other)

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

How old are people who do this job?

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 50 to 54 years. Of the whole working population 11.7% were aged 50 to 54 years. For people working as "production managers and directors in mining and energy", 15.8% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "production managers and directors in mining and energy" was 16 to 19 years.

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "production managers and directors in mining and energy", 6.1% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had more people aged between 30 and 49 years compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (91.6% compared with 8.4%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (87.2%) than self-employed (12.8%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Leeds, this is in the region of the Yorkshire & Humberside.
